title: SAP Business One client login fails with "License server is being configured; cannot connect" right after credentials are entered
msgKeys: License server is being configured; cannot connect
symptom: License server is being configured; cannot connect
rootCause:
Not verified in full — the KBA's cause section is behind an SAP support-portal login. Possibly: the License Manager / TAO NT Naming Service on the license server host is stopped, still initializing, or unreachable due to a firewall blocking port 30000; can also occur when the license server address configured on the client is wrong or points to a stale IP.

Source: SAP KBA 3495200; SAP Notes 1142479, 1658707, 1785166 per SAP Community references; Boyum IT partner support article on "Connection to license server failed".

solutions.label: Restart the license service and check port 30000
solutions.body:
On <host> (the license server), open Windows Services and restart "SAP Business One License Manager" (TAO NT Naming Service).
Confirm no firewall (Windows Firewall or network) is blocking TCP port 30000 between clients and <host>.
On an affected client, verify the license server address configured in the SAP Business One client (System Landscape Directory / License Manager settings) matches <host> exactly (not a stale IP/hostname).

Trade-off: restarting the license service briefly disconnects all currently-licensed users; do it during a maintenance window.

solutions.label: Validate the DI API local config file
solutions.body:
Check b1-local-machine.xml in the DI API installation folder for a literal "localhost" entry where the real license server address should be, and correct it.

Only relevant when the error originates from a DI API-based add-on rather than the SAP Business One client itself.

prevention: Set the License Manager/TAO NT Naming Service to Automatic (Delayed Start) so it comes up reliably after a server reboot, and document the license server's stable hostname/IP in the client configuration.

title: HTTP 403 on deploy: /UI5/ABAP_REPOSITORY_SRV not activated, or S_DEVELOP missing
symptom:
The deploy stops right at the start:

  Error: request failed with status code 403.

It never reaches the upload phase.
rootCause:
Two independent causes, both returning 403:

1. The OData service /UI5/ABAP_REPOSITORY_SRV is not activated on the ABAP system. The system answers 403 rather than 404 when the service is unavailable — which reads like an authorization problem but is not one.
2. The deploying user is missing the S_DEVELOP authorization object on the backend.

Not verified on our own systems — sourced from SAP-samples documentation and a community blog post.

solutions.label: Activate the service via /IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE (on-premise systems)
solutions.body:
1. Transaction: /n/IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE
2. System Alias: LOCAL
3. Technical Service Name: /UI5/*
4. Get Services -> select /UI5/ABAP_REPOSITORY_SRV -> Add
5. Assign a package ($TMP for development-only, or a transportable package)

After activation the service appears in SICF at:
  /sap/opu/odata/ui5/abap_repository_srv

Does not apply to S/4HANA Public Cloud, where the service ships activated — see solution 2.

solutions.label: Grant S_DEVELOP to the deploying user
solutions.body:
Ask Basis to grant the S_DEVELOP authorization object on the backend system.

On S/4HANA Public Cloud the equivalent is a Business Role containing the Developer Extensibility catalog — check it through the Maintain Business Roles app.

solutions.label: Tell a service 403 apart from an authorization 403
solutions.body:
Open this directly in the browser after signing in:
  https://<host>/sap/opu/odata/UI5/ABAP_REPOSITORY_SRV/?$format=json

- 403 for an admin user too -> the service is not activated
- 403 only for your user -> missing authorization

prevention: Put both conditions on the checklist for any new environment: /UI5/ABAP_REPOSITORY_SRV activated, and the deploying user holding S_DEVELOP (or the Developer Extensibility role on Cloud).

title: Deploy fails with "can only be deployed to the previous package" even though the package in ui5-deploy.yaml is correct
symptom:
`npm run deploy` fails with HTTP 400. The BSP upload phase runs fine; the failure lands in the Application Index step:

  Updating existing SAPUI5 ABAP repository ZQM04
  * Updating the Application Index *
  error Error updating LADIs for UI5 repository ZQM04, package ZQM04, transport HL8Kxxxxxx
  info  Inbound ZQM04-display was converted to LADI ZQM04_UI5R
  error SAPUI5 application can only be deployed to the previous package ZQM

The giveaway: changing `package` in ui5-deploy.yaml does not change the message, and neither does changing the transport.
rootCause:
The conflict is not on the BSP application. It is on the LADI (Launchpad App Descriptor Item) generated from the `crossNavigation` block in manifest.json.

The LADI name derives from the BSP repository name, not from the semantic object: repository `ZQM04` produces LADI `ZQM04_UI5R`. When a LADI of that name already exists — or once existed and was undeployed — under a different package, the Application Index step refuses to write it into the new package.

If the earlier deletion of that LADI sits in a transport that has not been released, the old package assignment is still recorded in the object directory, so the system keeps reading back the old package.

solutions.label: Remove crossNavigation from manifest.json to unblock the deploy
solutions.body:
Verified: the deploy succeeded immediately after removing this block.

Comment out or delete `crossNavigation` in webapp/manifest.json, then run `npm run deploy`. With no inbound there is no LADI to generate, so the Application Index step has nothing to conflict on.

The app is reachable at its direct URL:
  https://<host>/sap/bc/ui5_ui5/sap/<appname>/index.html

Trade-off: no tile on the Fiori Launchpad. Use this when you need to ship today.

solutions.label: Delete the stale LADI in ADT, then restore crossNavigation
solutions.body:
Not verified on this system.

1. ADT (Eclipse) -> Ctrl+Shift+A -> type <APPNAME>_UI5R
2. Note its Package and Transport
3. Delete -> assign to your transport -> Activate
4. Restore crossNavigation in manifest.json
5. npm run deploy

Requires delete authorization on the object (Developer Extensibility role). If the LADI belongs to someone else's transport and that transport is not released, you cannot delete it — the transport owner has to release it or delete the object themselves.

Note: SAP Community reports that deleting a LADI by hand in Eclipse is blocked on S/4HANA Public Cloud (message along the lines of "SAP GUI is not supported in project"). If you hit that, go to solution 5.

solutions.label: Release the transport that carries the LADI deletion
solutions.body:
Not verified.

Applies when the LADI was undeployed but the deletion still sits in an unreleased transport. Find that transport in the Transport Organizer, release it through the "Export Software Collection" app, then deploy again.

Warning: releasing pushes every object in that transport to the next system. Review its contents first, especially if the transport belongs to someone else.

solutions.label: Rename the BSP app so a fresh LADI is generated
solutions.body:
Not verified.

Change `app.name` in ui5-deploy.yaml (e.g. ZQM04 -> ZQM04A). That yields a new LADI `ZQM04A_UI5R` which does not collide with the old object. Keep crossNavigation as it is.

Trade-off: the app URL changes, the Business Catalog and Business Role assignments have to be redone, and the old app is left behind as clutter. Use this only when you have no ADT delete rights and cannot reach the transport owner.

solutions.label: Open an SAP incident under component CA-FLP-ABA-DT
solutions.body:
Outcome not verified.

This has been reported on SAP Community: redeploying a Fiori app a second time to S/4HANA Cloud hits a LADI error, and manual deletion is blocked. That thread has no resolution — the only recommendation given is to open an incident with SAP.

Component: CA-FLP-ABA-DT

Attach to the ticket:
- the full deploy log (run with log: 5)
- repository name, package, transport
- the Transaction ID from the Gateway Error Log
- what you already tried and what happened

Use this when solutions 2 and 3 are both out of reach and you need to keep the app name.

prevention:
Before undeploying an app that has crossNavigation, check which package and transport its LADI belongs to — and release the transport carrying the deletion before deploying again.

Agree a rule in the team: one owner per app, deploying with their own transport. Several people deploying the same app through different transports is exactly how this class of conflict appears.

Fix `app.name` and `package` by convention on the very first deploy. Neither can be changed afterwards.
refs: ADT Feed Reader -> SAP Gateway Error Log
SLG1 in client 000, object /UI5/APPIDX (backend admin only)
Object type: Launchpad App Descriptor Item (LADI)

title: ABAP program terminates with short dump TIME_OUT after exceeding maximum work process runtime
symptom:
Runtime Error: TIME_OUT
Short text: Time limit exceeded.
What happened?
The program "<program name>" has exceeded the maximum permitted runtime without
interruption and has therefore been terminated.
rootCause:
The dispatcher/work process aborts any step whose runtime exceeds profile parameter rdisp/scheduler/prio_high|normal|low/max_runtime (successor to rdisp/max_wprun_time). It is a protective timeout, usually triggered by an unindexed SELECT, a huge internal-table loop, or unexpectedly large production data volume.

Source: SAP Help "ABAP Runtime Errors and Short Dumps"; SAP KBA 2194355 (SAPLSENA case); SAP KBA 2772044 (SAPLSZA0/SAPLBUPA_SELECT case).

solutions.label: Analyze and fix the expensive statement
solutions.body:
Open the dump in ST22, note the program/include/line, then profile with SAT.
If a SELECT is the hotspot, run an ST05 SQL trace to find a missing index or bad WHERE clause and add a secondary index (needs a transport).
If it's a large loop, add package processing (SELECT ... PACKAGE SIZE) or early exits.

Durable fix; needs the process owner and possibly a DBA to validate index changes.

solutions.label: Raise the runtime limit as a stopgap
solutions.body:
In RZ10/RZ11 temporarily raise rdisp/scheduler/prio_high/max_runtime.

Only buys time; the performance problem remains and it still competes for work processes. Requires Basis and may need an instance restart.

prevention: Require an ST05/SQL trace review in the transport checklist for reports/jobs touching high-volume tables.

title: SAP Business One Integration Framework (B1i) clients/dashboards fail with "Cannot connect to SAP Business One Integration Service, in the Microsoft Service window make sure this service is running"
msgKeys: Cannot connect to SAP Business One Integration Service
make sure this service is running
symptom: Cannot connect to SAP Business One Integration Service, in the Microsoft Service window make sure this service is running
rootCause:
The Windows service "SAP Business One Integration Service" (B1i / Tomcat-based server) is stopped, failed to start, or its listening ports (8080/8443) are already bound by another program; a missing/corrupted Visual C++ redistributable on the host has also been reported to prevent the service from starting.

Source: SAP Note 1619422 "B1ic Troubleshooting Guide"; SAP Community/Answers threads on "Cannot connect to SAP Business One Integration Service".

solutions.label: Start the Integration Service and clear port conflicts
solutions.body:
On the B1i server host, open Windows Services and check "SAP Business One Integration Service" (and "Event Sender Service"); if stopped, start it and set Startup Type to Automatic.
If it fails to start, check for another process bound to TCP 8080/8443 (e.g. another Tomcat/IIS instance) and stop/reconfigure that process.
Confirm the Visual C++ redistributable required by the B1i installer is present and not corrupted; reinstall if needed.
Retry the client/dashboard connection.

Trade-off: restarting B1i interrupts any in-flight integration scenarios (DTW-style flows, intercompany, third-party middleware) until it's back up.

solutions.label: Re-run the integration component installer to repair DI Proxy
solutions.body:
If the service starts but connections still fail, re-run the SAP Business One integration package installer to repair the DI Proxy component, then restart the service.

More disruptive; use only if step 1 doesn't resolve it.

prevention: Set the SAP Business One Integration Service to Automatic (Delayed Start) startup, and reserve ports 8080/8443 exclusively for B1i on that host to avoid third-party service collisions.

title: Logging into an SAP Business One company right after restoring a database over an existing one with the same name fails with "Connection to the database is lost" (ODBC -1102)
msgKeys: Connection to the database is lost
symptom: Connection to the database is lost; contact your system administrator (ODBC -1102) (Message 131-183)
rootCause:
When a database is restored over (or with the same name as) an existing SAP Business One company, the System Landscape Directory (SLD) still holds the old database-user credentials/mapping for that company, which no longer match the restored database, so the client cannot log in.

Source: SAP Note 3303958 "Login Error When Restoring the Same Database".

solutions.label: Delete-then-restore and refresh the DB user in SLD
solutions.body:
Do not simply overwrite the existing company database with a restore. Instead:
Delete the old database (e.g. <company-db>) from SQL Server/HANA.
In the SLD control center, select the company and choose "Refresh Database User".
Restore the new backup using the same database name as the one just deleted.
Log in to the company as usual.

Trade-off: requires the company to be offline during the delete+restore window; skipping the "Refresh Database User" step reproduces the error even after a clean restore (confirmed as still required on FP 2305+ per the SAP Note).

solutions.label: Refresh DB user after any restore, even non-overwrite ones
solutions.body: As a safety habit, run SLD -> company -> "Refresh Database User" after every restore of that company's database, whether or not the name changed, since stale credential caching has been observed even in same-name restores on newer patch levels.

prevention: Make "SLD Refresh Database User" a standard, documented step in the DBA restore runbook for SAP Business One, not an optional afterthought.

title: Posting/reversal transactions dump with DBIF_RSQL_SQL_ERROR in READ_NRIV during number-range buffering
symptom:
Category: ABAP programming error
Runtime Error: DBIF_RSQL_SQL_ERROR
Exception: CX_SY_OPEN_SQL_DB
The termination occurred in the ABAP program "SAPLSNR3" in "READ_NRIV".
rootCause:
Not verified in full — the KBA's cause/solution text sits behind an SAP support-portal login; only the symptom text was confirmed directly. Per the KBA summary, the dump happens during posting/reversal/billing under number-range buffering (table NRIV, transaction SNRO); the deadlock/buffering keywords point to concurrent number-range buffer updates colliding at the database level.

Source: SAP KBA 1888646.

solutions.label: Apply KBA 1888646 guidance / adjust SNRO buffering
solutions.body:
Capture the exact SQL error text from ST22 (deadlock vs lock-wait timeout) and compare it to KBA 1888646.
Check the SNRO buffering mode for the affected number range object; switching to main-memory buffering trades a small gap risk for far fewer DB round trips, removing the contention window.

Needs SNRO change access; validate off-peak since it affects all users of that number range.

solutions.label: Retry and monitor
solutions.body: If it's a one-off transient DB deadlock, reprocess the failed document and watch ST22 for recurrence before changing buffering.

prevention: Review number-range buffering mode (buffered/main-memory) for any object with high-concurrency posting during design.

title: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway: the destination URL includes a service path
symptom: The deploy returns HTTP 502 Bad Gateway. The system is reachable but the response is not valid.
rootCause: Not verified on our own systems. Per SAP-samples documentation: the destination's URL field carries a service path, so the final request path ends up duplicated and points nowhere valid.

solutions.label: Set the destination URL to the hostname only
solutions.body:
The destination URL must be:
  https://<hostname>

No /sap/opu/odata/... and no other path segment.

solutions.label: Inspect the actual request path with DEBUG
solutions.body:
DEBUG=* npm run deploy

The correct path is:
  /sap/opu/odata/UI5/ABAP_REPOSITORY_SRV

If you see that segment twice, or appended after another path, the destination URL is the problem.

prevention: Standardise how destinations are declared in the project documentation: URL = hostname, never with a path.

title: HTTP 503: Cloud Connector cannot establish a tunnel to the backend
symptom: The deploy returns HTTP 503 with a message along the lines of: Cloud Connector cannot establish secure tunnel to back end.
rootCause: Not verified on our own systems. Per SAP-samples documentation: the SAP Cloud Connector cannot reach the on-premise backend system.

solutions.label: Check the Cloud Connector state
solutions.body:
1. Open the Cloud Connector admin UI and confirm the subaccount shows as Connected
2. Under Cloud To On-Premise, confirm the backend is listed with the right virtual host
3. Use the Cloud Connector's Check Availability function

solutions.label: Rule out a local firewall or proxy
solutions.body: A corporate firewall or proxy can block the connection. Try from a different network, or ask IT to open the relevant port.

prevention: Verify Cloud Connector reachability when setting up a new team member's environment, before handing them deployment work.

title: Object Page shows only the generated "General Information" section — facets defined by CDS @UI.facet never render, with no error anywhere
symptom:
No error is raised anywhere: the CDS objects activate, the service responds, the browser console is clean, and $metadata contains the navigation property.

The Object Page renders only the facet declared by the app's own annotation file — typically a single "General Information" section — while the facets declared in the backend CDS metadata extension (@UI.facet, for example a #LINEITEM_REFERENCE section pointing at a composition child) never appear.

The decisive artefact is in webapp/annotations/annotation.xml:

<Annotations Target="SAP__self.ZC_<ROOT>Type">
  <Annotation Term="UI.Facets">
    <Collection>
      <Record Type="UI.ReferenceFacet">
        <PropertyValue Property="ID" String="GeneratedFacet1"/>
        <PropertyValue Property="Label" String="General Information"/>
        <PropertyValue Property="Target" AnnotationPath="@UI.FieldGroup#GeneratedGroup"/>

The string GeneratedFacet1 is the giveaway.
rootCause:
Front-end annotations override back-end annotations on a term-by-term basis. When webapp/annotations/annotation.xml declares the term UI.Facets for the same target entity type, it replaces the entire UI.Facets value coming from the service metadata — the two collections are not merged record by record. Every facet defined by @UI.facet in the CDS metadata extension is therefore discarded before rendering, and only the facets listed in the local file survive.

The local file is usually not hand-written. @sap/generator-fiori scaffolds annotation.xml with a UI.FieldGroup#GeneratedGroup and a single UI.ReferenceFacet with ID GeneratedFacet1 when the service carries no UI annotations at generation time. It then keeps overriding the backend silently once CDS annotations are added later, which is why the problem surfaces long after the app was generated and why nothing in the backend looks wrong.

A second, independent cause produces a similar-looking symptom: the section does render, but its table stays empty because the target entity of a #LINEITEM_REFERENCE facet has no @UI.lineItem annotations. Establish which of the two applies before changing anything — if no section appears at all it is the override; if an empty section appears it is the missing @UI.lineItem.

Source: SAPUI5 documentation, "Working with OData Annotations" — "When an annotation term, such as UI.LineItem, is defined in an additional annotation source on the front end, it overwrites the annotation term which is defined in the back end (CDS), if one exists" and "front-end annotations override back-end annotations on a term-by-term basis". The precedence rule is documented; the fix below was derived from a real project's artefacts but has not been re-executed and confirmed on a system, hence verified: false.

solutions.label: Delete the generated UI.Facets block from the app's local annotation file
solutions.body:
Open webapp/annotations/annotation.xml and remove the <Annotations Target="SAP__self.<ENTITY>Type"> block that declares UI.Facets, together with the UI.FieldGroup#GeneratedGroup it points at if nothing else references it.

Keep the file and its edmx:Reference headers with an empty Schema, so the manifest datasource stays valid and SAP Fiori tools wizards still have somewhere to write:

  <edmx:DataServices>
    <!-- UI annotations are maintained in the backend CDS metadata extensions.
         Do not add UI.Facets here: it overrides the CDS definition. -->
    <Schema xmlns="http://docs.oasis-open.org/odata/ns/edm" Namespace="local"/>
  </edmx:DataServices>

Leave manifest.json alone — the "annotation" entry under dataSources and in mainService.settings.annotations can stay, it simply contributes nothing now.

Redeploy, or restart the local preview, then hard-refresh the browser (Ctrl+Shift+R): UI5 caches annotations and a stale cache makes a correct fix look like it did nothing.

Cost: none beyond a redeploy. No backend change, no transport, no downtime.

solutions.label: Keep the front end authoritative and re-declare every facet locally
solutions.body:
Only if the backend service is owned by another team and cannot be changed.

The local UI.Facets collection then has to list every facet the page needs, including the ones already declared by @UI.facet in CDS, because the local term replaces the backend term wholesale.

The facet list is maintained in two places from that point on and will drift. Treat this as a workaround, not a design.

solutions.label: If the section now appears but its table is empty, annotate the target entity
solutions.body:
A facet of type #LINEITEM_REFERENCE with targetElement '<association>' resolves to <association>/@UI.LineItem on the target entity. When that entity carries no @UI.lineItem, the section renders with no columns.

Create a metadata extension for the target CDS projection view with @UI.lineItem on the fields to display. The view must have @Metadata.allowExtensions: true. If the app has a sub-object-page route for that entity, add @UI.facet and @UI.identification there as well, otherwise the sub-page opens blank.

Before doing any of this, open the service's $metadata and confirm the NavigationProperty actually exists under the root EntityType. If it is missing, the problem is upstream — the child entity is not exposed in the service definition, or the composition/redirect in the projection view is wrong — and no amount of UI annotation will help.

prevention:
Choose one side as the source of truth for UI annotations. For a RAP service that means the backend CDS metadata extension; the app's local annotation.xml then stays empty apart from a comment saying so. Leaving the generator's scaffolded facet in place is the whole cause.

Re-check annotation.xml after running any SAP Fiori tools wizard (Add Page, Guided Development), since those write into that file and can reintroduce a UI.Facets term.

When a section defined in CDS does not appear and nothing anywhere reports an error, read the local annotation file before re-checking the CDS view, the service definition or the composition — the silent override looks exactly like a backend modelling mistake and sends people to the wrong layer for hours.

title: Fiori app fails with HTTP 404 "Resource not found for the segment '<segment>'" after an OData/CDS metadata change
msgKeys: Resource not found for the segment
symptom:
Resource not found for the segment '<segment>'
HTTP response status code: 404
rootCause:
Not verified in full — the source KBA's cause/solution text sits behind an SAP support-portal login; only the title/summary was accessible. Possibly: after a change to the underlying CDS view, RAP behavior definition, or SEGW/Gateway service, the Gateway/OData metadata cache still reflects the old model, so a request for a field/segment that changed or was removed returns 404 even though the backend model was updated.

Source: SAP KBA 2743849 "Resource not found for the segment 'XXXXXXXX'"; corroborated by an SAP Community thread with the same symptom.

solutions.label: Clear the Gateway/OData metadata cache and republish the service
solutions.body:
Run transaction /IWFND/CACHE_CLEANUP and /IWBEP/CACHE_CLEANUP on the relevant system(s) to purge stale metadata.
For a RAP-based OData V4 service, re-publish the Service Binding in ADT (right-click -> Publish) so the runtime regenerates $metadata.
Reload the Fiori app afterward.

Trade-off: a full cache clear can briefly affect other apps sharing the same Gateway hub, so schedule it outside peak hours if the hub is shared.

solutions.label: Diagnose the exact missing segment first
solutions.body:
Reproduce the request in /IWFND/GW_CLIENT and check /IWFND/ERROR_LOG for the failing timestamp to see exactly which segment/property is not found.
Confirm the CDS view/behavior definition/service definition still exposes that field or association; if it was intentionally renamed/removed, the frontend app also needs to be updated to match.

prevention: Add a mandatory "clear OData metadata cache" step to the deployment checklist whenever a CDS view, behavior definition, or service definition exposed via OData changes its exposed fields/associations.

title: App deploys fine but cannot reach its OData service
symptom:
The app renders but shows no data. The network tab reports 404 or 403 on /sap/opu/odata/...

It works locally (npm start) because the request goes through the ui5 middleware proxy.
rootCause:
Not verified. Common possibilities:
- the service is not published/activated on the tenant
- a Communication Arrangement is missing (for custom services on Public Cloud)
- the user lacks authorization for the service
- the `dataSource` uri in manifest.json points somewhere wrong

solutions.label: Call the service URL directly in the browser
solutions.body:
Take the uri from sap.app.dataSources in manifest.json, prepend the tenant host, and open it after signing in.

- 404 -> the service does not exist or is not activated
- 403 -> the service exists but the user lacks authorization
- 200 -> the problem is on the app side; check the manifest

solutions.label: Check the Communication Arrangement
solutions.body: Not verified for your specific case. On S/4HANA Public Cloud, exposing a service usually requires a matching Communication Scenario and Communication Arrangement. Check via the Communication Arrangements app.

solutions.label: Diff the deployed manifest against the repo
solutions.body: Open the manifest.json of the deployed app (through the app URL) and compare it with the one in the repository. Different uris mean the build used a mock configuration or a stale dist folder.

prevention: Keep the mock configuration (ui5-mock.yaml) clearly separate from the real one. Before handover, always test the app on the real tenant with an end-user account, not a developer account.

title: Package is not found on ABAP system when deploying a new app
msgKeys: Package is found on ABAP system (fail)
symptom: The deploy validation phase reports that the package declared in `app.package` of ui5-deploy.yaml does not exist.
rootCause: Not verified. Possibilities: the package was never created in ADT, the name is misspelled, or the package belongs to a software component the user has no rights on.

solutions.label: Create the package in ADT before deploying
solutions.body:
ADT -> select the parent package (e.g. ZQM) -> New -> ABAP Package -> set the name, Software Component and Transport Layer per project standard.

On S/4HANA Public Cloud the package must sit under a structure package that permits Developer Extensibility.

solutions.label: Use an existing parent package
solutions.body:
If you do not need a dedicated package per app, declare the parent package (e.g. ZQM) in ui5-deploy.yaml.

Note: the package of a BSP app cannot be changed after the first deploy.

prevention: Agree the package tree per business module at project start (ZQM, ZMM, ZSD...) and write it into the technical design. Avoid one package per app — it produces many near-empty packages and complicates transport bundling.

title: RAP business object create/update fails at runtime with CX_RAP_HANDLER_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
symptom:
Uncaught Exception CX_RAP_HANDLER_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
Handler not implemented; Method: &1, Involved Entities: &2
rootCause:
The behavior definition declares an operation/feature (e.g. FOR CREATE, FOR INSTANCE AUTHORIZATION, a custom action, draft handling) but the corresponding local handler method is missing or not activated in the behavior implementation class, so the RAP runtime cannot dispatch the call. This is documented RAP runtime message 006.

Source: SAP Community threads on RAP "handler not implemented" and instance authorization on create; message text corroborated by the RAP runtime message reference.

solutions.label: Implement the missing handler method
solutions.body:
In ADT, open the behavior definition and note every operation/feature declared (CREATE, UPDATE, an authorization control, a custom action, draft actions).
Open the behavior implementation class (local handler class inheriting CL_ABAP_BEHAVIOR_HANDLER, referenced by "implementation in class <behavior_implementation_class> unique") and add/complete the corresponding METHODS/handler for each declared operation.
Activate the behavior definition and the class together, then re-test the app action that failed.

solutions.label: Remove the declared operation/feature if it is not actually needed
solutions.body:
If the operation was declared by mistake (e.g. @AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #CHECK added but no authorization logic is needed yet), remove that clause from the behavior definition instead of leaving an unimplemented stub.

Trade-off: this disables the feature for all consumers until it is properly implemented later.

prevention: Always activate the behavior definition and its implementation class in the same step; use the ADT quick-fix to generate stub methods for every declared operation so nothing is silently left unimplemented.

title: Deploy to S/4HANA Public Cloud fails at authentication (reentranceTicket)
symptom: The deploy stops before the upload phase, or the browser opens and never returns, or it reports 401/403.
rootCause: Not verified. Possibilities: an expired session, a misconfigured BTP destination, declaring both `destination` and `url` so the target is ambiguous, or the business user missing the Developer Extensibility role.

solutions.label: Declare one target source, not two
solutions.body:
The deploy tooling prefers `destination` over `url`. For local development in VS Code with reentranceTicket you usually only need:

  target:
    url: https://<tenant>.s4hana.cloud.sap
    authenticationType: reentranceTicket

Use `destination` when running through BTP or CI. Declaring both makes debugging ambiguous.

solutions.label: Check the business user's role
solutions.body: The deploying user needs a Business Role containing the Developer Extensibility catalog (related to SAP_CORE_BC_EXT_TST). Ask an admin to check via the Maintain Business Roles app.

solutions.label: Sign in to the tenant before deploying
solutions.body: Open the tenant in a browser and sign in first, so the reentrance ticket has a valid session to pick up.

prevention: State it plainly in the project README: which environment uses `destination`, which uses `url`, and which roles are required to deploy.

title: SAPUI5 ABAP Repository with name Z... already exists
symptom: The first deploy of an app reports that a repository with that name already exists on the system, even though you have never deployed this app.
rootCause:
Not verified. BSP repository names are unique system-wide. Likely causes: a colleague already deployed an app under the same name, or an app left over from an earlier project.

Tell it apart from the LADI package conflict: this one blocks at repository creation (POST), while the LADI error blocks at the Application Index step after the upload has already completed.

solutions.label: Check the existing repository on the system
solutions.body:
Open this in the browser after signing in:

  https://<host>/sap/opu/odata/UI5/ABAP_REPOSITORY_SRV/Repositories('<APPNAME>')?$format=json

The response gives Package, Description and who created it. This is the only reliable source — do not go by memory.

solutions.label: Rename your app
solutions.body: If the existing app is still in use, change `app.name` in ui5-deploy.yaml to a name that is not taken.

solutions.label: Take over the existing app (if it really is yours)
solutions.body:
Keep the name and declare the package that repository actually belongs to — the deploy then switches from create to update mode.

Note: the package of an existing repository cannot be changed.

prevention: Keep a team-wide app name register (name — package — owner — environment) and check it before naming a new app. Prefix by module: ZQM01, ZQM02, and so on.

title: SM59 connection test fails with "timeout during allocate" / no connect of TP sapdp00
symptom:
ERROR: timeout during allocate
DETAIL: no connect of TP sapdp00 from host <host> after 20 sec
RETURN CODE 242
rootCause:
Not verified in full — the KBA's cause/solution text sits behind an SAP support-portal login; only the symptom text was confirmed directly. Per the KBA summary and related notes, this means the gateway could not reach the partner dispatcher (sapdpNN) within the allocate timeout — typically a blocked network path/firewall, the target instance being down, or (for locally-started RFC servers) gateway launch configuration.

Source: SAP KBA 3619529; SAP Note 638701; SAP Note 948636.

solutions.label: Verify network path and gateway, then retest
solutions.body:
In SM59 run Connection Test and note the exact host/port in the DETAIL line.
From the app server OS, test connectivity to <host>:33<NN> (sapdpNN) and the gateway port; loop in the network/firewall team if blocked.
Confirm the target instance/gateway is up (SM51, SMGW).
For locally-started RFC servers, check parameter rfc/use_gwstart per SAP Notes 638701 / 948636.

Basis + network team; low risk, but a gateway restart may be needed to pick up parameter changes.

solutions.label: Increase allocate timeout as stopgap
solutions.body: Only if the target is merely slow (not unreachable) — raising the timeout on a genuinely blocked path just delays the same failure.

prevention: Add a scheduled SM59 connection-test/RFC ping job for business-critical destinations so network changes are caught before they break integrations.

title: Background jobs stay Released/Ready with "No free batch work processes available" and never start
msgKeys: No free batch work processes available
symptom:
Job status: Released
Reason for Delay: No free batch work processes available
rootCause:
Not verified in full — the KBA's cause/solution text sits behind an SAP support-portal login; only the symptom text was confirmed directly. Per the KBA summary, the periodic scheduler check found no free BTC work process to dispatch to — commonly all BTC processes occupied by long-running jobs, too few BTC processes configured for the parallel job load, or a stale count vs SM50.

Source: SAP KBA 3148846; SAP KBA 3429310 (SM50-mismatch variant); SAP KBA 3008195 (FAQ).

solutions.label: Free up or add BTC work processes
solutions.body:
In SM50/SM66 identify what's occupying BTC processes; cancel genuinely stuck jobs with owner sign-off.
If under-provisioned, increase rdisp/wp_no_btc via RZ10/RZ11 — needs Basis and a maintenance window/instance restart.
Re-check SM37; Released jobs pick up automatically once a BTC process frees.

solutions.label: Reschedule to a quieter window
solutions.body: If contention is time-bound (e.g. during a HANA backup), shift the job's start time or use RZ04 operation modes/job classes instead of adding capacity.

prevention: Track daily BTC work-process peak utilization and revisit rdisp/wp_no_btc sizing whenever new recurring jobs are onboarded.

title: Deploy succeeds but no tile appears on the Fiori Launchpad
symptom: The deploy reports success and the app runs at its direct URL (/sap/bc/ui5_ui5/sap/<app>/index.html), but users do not see a tile in the Launchpad.
rootCause:
Not fully verified. Deploy only creates the BSP app and the LADI; a visible tile additionally requires the whole assignment chain: LADI -> Business Catalog -> Business Role -> Business User.

Two common breaks:
- manifest.json has no crossNavigation, so no LADI is generated
- the LADI exists but was never added to a catalog or role

solutions.label: Walk the assignment chain in order
solutions.body:
1. Does manifest.json contain sap.app.crossNavigation.inbounds?
2. Does LADI <APPNAME>_UI5R exist in ADT?
3. Custom Catalog Extensions app: has the app been added to a Business Catalog?
4. Maintain Business Roles app: has that catalog been assigned to the user's role?

Stop at the first step that fails — later steps are meaningless until it passes.

solutions.label: Clear the user's Launchpad cache
solutions.body: Not verified. If everything is assigned correctly and the tile still does not appear, sign out and back in, or open the Launchpad in a private window to rule out browser caching.

prevention: Put those four steps in the Definition of Done for every Fiori app. A successful deploy does not mean a usable app.

title: Deploy fails because the transport request is released or belongs to another package
symptom: The deploy stops at the validation phase with a message about the transport request: not found, or not writable.
rootCause:
Not verified. Common possibilities:
- the transport has been released and can no longer be written to
- the transport belongs to a different package than the target
- the transport belongs to another owner who has not granted write access
- a Customizing request was used where a Workbench request is required

solutions.label: Check the transport status in ADT
solutions.body:
Window -> Show View -> Transport Organizer -> find the transport number.

Confirm: status = Modifiable, type = Workbench Request, and that you are the owner or have write access.

solutions.label: Create a new transport
solutions.body: If the old transport is released, create a new Workbench Request in ADT and update `app.transport` in ui5-deploy.yaml.

solutions.label: Do not borrow someone else's transport
solutions.body: Your objects end up mixed into their request; when they release it, your unfinished code rides along to QA or PRD. Always use your own transport unless there is an explicit agreement.

prevention: One Workbench Request per developer per sprint. Record the transport number in the project README so the team knows which app travels in which request.
refs: Fiori app: Export Software Collection (S/4HANA Public Cloud)

title: undeploy leaves secondary objects behind — the app is gone but the next deploy still conflicts
symptom: After `npm run undeploy` the BSP app is gone, yet the next deploy still fails with a package or LADI error naming that same app.
rootCause: Not verified. Hypothesis: undeploy removes the BSP repository, but the deletion of secondary objects — the LADI in particular — is recorded in a transport. While that transport stays unreleased, the old record remains in the object directory and collides on the next deploy.

solutions.label: Check for leftover objects before deploying again
solutions.body:
After every undeploy, look in ADT for:
- BSP application <APPNAME>
- LADI <APPNAME>_UI5R

Note the package and transport of anything still sitting in a deleted-pending state.

solutions.label: Release the transport carrying the deletion before redeploying
solutions.body:
Not verified. Release the transport so the deletion is committed, then deploy again.

Review the transport contents first — it may carry someone else's objects.

prevention:
Treat undeploy as an operation with lasting consequences, not a clean slate. If you only need to change the app content, deploy over it instead.

When you must undeploy: use your own transport, write down the number, and release it before deploying the same app name again.

title: CDS view activation fails with "Use of annotation 'ObjectModel.compositionRoot' is not permitted (not released)" in ABAP Cloud
symptom:
Syntax error during CDS DDL activation:
Use of annotation 'ObjectModel.compositionRoot' is not permitted (not released)
rootCause:
The classic ObjectModel.* annotations belong to the older BOPF-based "ABAP Programming Model for SAP Fiori" and are not released for the ABAP Cloud development model (S/4HANA Cloud ABAP Environment / BTP ABAP Environment, formerly "Embedded Steampunk") — only the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) is released there.

Source: SAP Community blog "Embedded Steampunk – What's under the hood Part II"; corroborated by an SAP Community thread on the same CDS annotation error.

solutions.label: Re-model the business object with RAP instead of legacy ObjectModel annotations
solutions.body:
Remove the ObjectModel.compositionRoot / ObjectModel.association.type annotations from the CDS view.
Create a Behavior Definition for the root entity and model compositions using RAP's "composition" syntax in the CDS association plus root/composition-child declarations in the BDEF instead of the BOPF-oriented annotations.
Activate the CDS view + BDEF + service definition/binding as a RAP business object.

solutions.label: Keep the legacy-annotated view out of ABAP Cloud packages
solutions.body: If the object genuinely must stay on the classic (on-premise, non-cloud) programming model, keep it in a package/system that is not exposed to the ABAP Cloud development model, since ObjectModel.* + BOPF is not supported there at all.

prevention: Run the ATC "Cloud readiness"/released-API check on any CDS view copied from an on-premise template before moving it into an S/4HANA Cloud or BTP ABAP Environment package.

title: DI API call fails with "DI Error: (-2028) No matching records found (ODBC -2028) - The di call #1 did fail" when adding/updating a document
symptom: DI Error: (-2028) No matching records found (ODBC -2028)-The di call #1 did fail
rootCause:
A field value set by the calling code references a master-data key (e.g. CardCode, ItemCode, SalesPersonCode, VendorNum) that does not exist in its target table, OR the code manually populated a field that DI API normally auto-fills (Line.ItemCode, Line.VendorNum, Line.ItemDescription, Line.ShipDate, PaymentGroupCode), which then fails DI's internal lookup.

Source: SAP KBA 3133909, SAP KBA 3075050, SAP KBA 2650591; SAP Community thread "No matching records found (ODBC -2028)".

solutions.label: Remove DI-managed fields and validate referenced codes
solutions.body:
Strip out any fields in the request payload that DI API auto-populates (Line.ItemCode, Line.VendorNum, Line.ItemDescription, Line.ShipDate, PaymentGroupCode) and let DI derive them.
Before calling Add/Update, verify every referenced master-data code (CardCode, ItemCode, SalesPersonCode, WhsCode, AcctCode) actually exists in <company-db> via a lookup call.
Re-run the DI call with only the minimal required fields set.

Trade-off: requires an extra read call per master-data reference, adding latency to bulk imports.

solutions.label: Bisect the payload
solutions.body:
Remove fields from the failing request one at a time (starting with optional/derived ones) until the call succeeds, to isolate which specific code is invalid.

Useful for one-off debugging but not for production error handling.

prevention: Validate all foreign-key style codes (BP, item, sales employee, warehouse) against SAP Business One before submission in any DI API/DTW integration, and avoid manually setting fields DI API is documented to auto-fill.

title: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout when deploying a large app
symptom: The deploy runs for a while and then stops with HTTP 504. Usually with apps that have many files, or on a loaded system.
rootCause: Not verified on our own systems. Per SAP-samples documentation: the backend response time exceeds the timeout configured on the destination.

solutions.label: Raise HTML5.Timeout on the destination
solutions.body:
Add or edit the destination property in the BTP cockpit:

  HTML5.Timeout = 60000

Milliseconds. 60000 is the documented minimum; larger apps may need more.

solutions.label: Shrink the archive
solutions.body: Review the `exclude` block in ui5-deploy.yaml — drop /test/, /localService/, mock data and anything else not needed at runtime. The deploy log prints the file count in the archive; use it to compare before and after.

prevention: Set HTML5.Timeout = 60000 when creating any new destination, rather than waiting to hit the error.

title: Error in the SAPUI5 repository, which is a local object of the user xxx
symptom: Deploying from SAP Business Application Studio or VS Code fails with a message saying the repository is a local object belonging to another user.
rootCause: Not verified. Likely: the repository was created earlier in package $TMP (a local object) by a different user. Local objects are bound to the user who created them and cannot be shared.

solutions.label: Deploy to a transportable package instead of $TMP
solutions.body:
$TMP is for personal throwaway experiments only. Anything shared must live in a Z* package with a transport.

Note: once created in $TMP the package cannot be changed — the object has to be deleted and recreated, or a different name used.

solutions.label: Ask the owner to delete the local object
solutions.body: Only the user who created a local object can delete it in ADT. After deletion, deploy again into a transportable package.

prevention: Ban $TMP for any app another person will use or that will move to QA. Add it to the code review checklist: verify `app.package` in ui5-deploy.yaml.

title: Saving/editing a RAP draft-enabled Fiori Elements app fails with HTTP 412 Precondition Failed
symptom:
PATCH/POST to the draft or active instance returns HTTP 412 Precondition Failed
If-Match header value sent by the client does not match the current ETag on the server
rootCause:
In RAP, the field designated as (total) etag master must be kept current by the behavior implementation's FOR READ method (and, for unmanaged save, updated on every MODIFY). If that method does not return/refresh the current etag value, the framework's ETag comparison mismatches even though no other user actually changed the data, and the request is rejected with 412 as if a concurrent edit occurred.

Source: SAP Community blogs "ETag In RAP" and "Handling 412 Precondition Failed and 428 Precondition Required Errors in SAP APIs Using ETag".

solutions.label: Complete the FOR READ implementation so it always returns the current etag field
solutions.body:
In the behavior implementation class, implement (or fix) the FOR READ method so it always returns the up-to-date value of the field annotated as etag master / total etag, sourced from the database or an EML READ.
For unmanaged save scenarios, ensure the field is also explicitly updated on every MODIFY so the stored value and the value returned to the client stay in sync.
Retest the create/edit/save cycle end-to-end, including concurrent-edit scenarios, since a real 412 should still occur when another user genuinely changed the record.

solutions.label: Unblock a stuck user session
solutions.body:
As a temporary workaround, have the user close and reopen (GET again) the object to fetch a fresh ETag before retrying the edit.

This does not fix the underlying code defect.

prevention: Add ABAP Unit tests (RAP Test Double Framework) that assert the etag/total-etag field is returned by FOR READ and updated by MODIFY, so a missing etag refresh is caught before transport/deploy.

title: unable to get local issuer certificate when deploying from VS Code
msgKeys: unable to get local issuer certificate
symptom:
The deploy fails with a TLS certificate error, typically "unable to get local issuer certificate" or "self signed certificate in certificate chain".

Common with on-premise systems using an internal corporate certificate.
rootCause: Not verified on our own systems. Node.js does not trust a certificate issued by an internal CA because that CA is not in Node's default trust store.

solutions.label: Register the internal CA with Node.js
solutions.body:
Get the corporate CA file from IT, then:

  export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/company-ca.pem
  npm run deploy

Windows PowerShell:
  $env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS="C:\path\company-ca.pem"

This is the correct fix: TLS verification stays fully in place, you only add a CA you trust.

solutions.label: Disable certificate checking (local DEV only)
solutions.body:
In ui5-deploy.yaml:

  configuration:
    strictSsl: false

Do NOT use this on CI/CD or any shared environment, and do not commit it to the main branch — it switches off server identity verification entirely.

prevention: Distribute the internal CA file and the NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS instruction as part of onboarding, instead of leaving each developer to disable strictSsl on their own.

title: SAP Business One Service Layer rejects every subsequent OData call with an "Invalid session or session already timeout" error after a successful login
msgKeys: Invalid session or session already timeout
symptom: Invalid session or session already timeout
rootCause:
Not verified. Possibly: the B1SESSION cookie issued at /Login expires (default idle timeout is short) or is dropped/mismatched with the ROUTEID cookie when Service Layer sits behind a load balancer with multiple worker processes, so the next request is routed to a worker that never saw the session.

Source: SAP KBA 3383703; SAP Community thread "The B1 Service Layer sends the error 'Invalid session' randomly".

solutions.label: Re-login and always forward both session cookies
solutions.body:
Ensure the integration client stores BOTH the B1SESSION and ROUTEID cookies returned by POST /b1s/v1/Login and replays both on every subsequent call.
Increase SessionTimeout in the Service Layer config (b1s.conf) if calls are naturally spaced further apart than the default.
Restart the b1s (Service Layer) service after config changes.

Trade-off: raising the timeout keeps sessions open longer, slightly increasing memory use per idle session on the Service Layer host.

solutions.label: Implement automatic re-login on 401
solutions.body:
Catch the 401/"Invalid session" response in the client and transparently call Login again before retrying the original request.

Adds latency to the first failed call but avoids manual intervention.

prevention: Design integrations to detect session-expiry responses and re-authenticate automatically rather than assuming a session stays valid for the life of a batch job.

title: Deploy succeeds but the browser still loads the old version of the app
symptom: The deploy reports success but the app still shows the old UI or logic. Or the deploy log marks every file "Already up-to-date" even though you just changed the code.
rootCause:
Not fully verified. Two layers can cause it:
- the build reused a stale dist folder, so the archive never contained the change (the log then says Already up-to-date)
- cachebuster or browser cache is holding the old version on the client side

solutions.label: Identify the layer from the deploy log
solutions.body:
Read the `* Operations *` block (needs log: 5 or --verbose):

- every file "Already up-to-date" -> the problem is in the build, not the browser cache
- files marked UPDATE/ADD -> the upload was correct; the problem is client-side

solutions.label: Build clean
solutions.body:
npm run build -- --clean-dest

Or delete the dist folder by hand and rebuild.

solutions.label: Check the browser side
solutions.body:
Open the app in a private window, or hard reload (Ctrl+Shift+R). If the new version appears, it was the client cache.

Verify that the generateCachebusterInfo task runs in ui5.yaml — deploy-to-abap is normally placed with afterTask: generateCachebusterInfo for exactly this reason.

prevention: Before telling a client the new version is live, check it yourself in a private window. In the deploy log, read the Operations block to confirm files were actually written.

title: deploy --testMode reports "no problems" but the real deploy still fails with 400
symptom:
`npm run deploy-test` reports:

  OK SAPUI5 ABAP Repository follows the rules of creating BSP application
  OK Package is found on ABAP system
  OK Transport Request is found on ABAP system
  Test run has indicated no problems

But `npm run deploy` right afterwards still fails with status 400.
rootCause:
Test mode only runs configuration validation and simulates the file upload. It does NOT run the "Updating the Application Index" step and does not write LADIs — which is exactly where most real deployment failures occur.

The deploy tooling log says so itself: "A successful TestMode execution does not necessarily mean that your upload will be successful."

solutions.label: Know what test mode actually covers
solutions.body:
Test mode checks: yaml syntax, package exists, transport exists, connectivity and authentication, archive structure.

Test mode does NOT check: writing to the transport, the Application Index, LADIs, repository registration, package conflicts on secondary objects.

Treat it as a fast pre-filter, not a guarantee.

solutions.label: Read the log at the right phase when a real deploy fails
solutions.body:
Skip the header and the Parameters block. Find the line `* Updating the Application Index *` — the real error is always right after it.

The `info ... message_text ...` lines are just links to look up message text, not errors.

prevention: When deploying an app for the first time, or after changing the manifest, run a real deploy on DEV. Never let a passing test mode decide a promotion to QA.

title: prebuild fails: tsc --noEmit reports type errors after updating @sapui5/types
symptom: `npm run deploy` stops at the prebuild step with TypeScript errors, although the code has not changed — you only ran npm install or updated a dependency.
rootCause: Not verified. Likely: @sapui5/types uses a version range (~1.142.0), so npm install pulled a newer patch with different type definitions; or the types version drifted away from the app's minUI5Version.

solutions.label: Compare the types version against minUI5Version
solutions.body:
The deploy log prints minUI5Version (e.g. 1.142.12). Compare it with @sapui5/types in package.json.

Pin an exact version to stop the drift:
  "@sapui5/types": "1.142.0"

Then: rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && npm install

solutions.label: Restore from package-lock.json
solutions.body:
If package-lock.json is in git and the build worked before:
  git checkout package-lock.json && npm ci

npm ci installs exactly what the lock file says and never upgrades.

solutions.label: Read the actual type errors
solutions.body:
npm run ts-typecheck

Run it on its own to see the full error list instead of a truncated slice in the deploy log.

prevention: Commit package-lock.json and use npm ci on build machines and CI. Pin exact versions for @sapui5/types and @ui5/cli rather than using ^ or ~ ranges — these packages change type definitions between patch releases.

title: Files silently skipped: "Not uploaded as binary/text type is unknown"
symptom:
The deploy succeeds but some files never reach the system. The log lists them with a note along the lines of "Not uploaded as binary/text type is unknown".

Result: a missing font, a missing config file, or a 404 on one specific resource at runtime.
rootCause: Not verified on our own systems. Per SAP-samples documentation: the file extension is not in the SAPUI5 ABAP Repository's default recognition list, so the upload skips it.

solutions.label: Declare the extensions in the recognition lists
solutions.body:
Create these files in the webapp/ folder:

  .Ui5RepositoryTextFiles     - for text files (.json, .xml, .properties, .svg...)
  .Ui5RepositoryBinaryFiles   - for binary files (.woff2, .png, .pdf...)

One extension per line. Then build and deploy again.

solutions.label: Compare the archive contents against the operations list
solutions.body: Set log: 5 in ui5-deploy.yaml. Look at the "Adding <file>" lines when the archive is created and the `* Operations *` block on upload. A file present in the archive but absent from Operations is the one being skipped.

prevention: When adding a new asset type to a project (fonts, icons, config files), verify it actually reached the system rather than trusting the "Deployment successful" line.

title: How to enable network-level debugging on a deploy
symptom: A deploy fails and it is unclear where the request actually goes, what headers it carries, or how it redirects — especially when you suspect the destination, a proxy or a certificate.
rootCause: The deploy tooling's default log does not cover the HTTP layer. Node.js debugging has to be switched on.

solutions.label: Mac / Linux
solutions.body:
DEBUG=* NODE_DEBUG=http,https,net,tls npm run deploy 2>&1 | tee deploy-debug.log

Then search the file for:
- the actual request path (it must contain /sap/opu/odata/UI5/ABAP_REPOSITORY_SRV)
- the returned status code
- any TLS error

solutions.label: Windows PowerShell
solutions.body: $env:DEBUG="*"; $env:NODE_DEBUG="http,https,net,tls"; npm run deploy 2>&1 | Tee-Object deploy-debug.log

prevention:
Attach deploy-debug.log whenever you open a ticket with Basis or SAP — it cuts the round trips considerably.

Security note: this log can contain tokens or session cookies. Review it before sending it anywhere, and never commit it.

title: Turning on detailed logging for deploy-to-abap
symptom: A deploy fails but the default log (Info level) does not show the payload sent, nor which package and transport were actually used.
rootCause: The default log level for deploy-to-abap is Info (2). The payload, the resolved configuration and the archive file list only appear at Debug/Silly level.

solutions.label: Add log: 5 to ui5-deploy.yaml
solutions.body:
Place it at the same level as target and app:

  - name: deploy-to-abap
    afterTask: generateCachebusterInfo
    configuration:
      log: 5
      target: { ... }
      app: { ... }

Levels: 0 Error / 1 Warn / 2 Info (default) / 3 Verbose / 4 Debug / 5 Silly.
Equivalent: verbose: true.

solutions.label: Use the CLI instead of editing the yaml
solutions.body:
npm run build && npx fiori deploy --config ui5-deploy.yaml --verbose

Keep the output:
  npm run deploy 2>&1 | tee deploy-debug.log

prevention: Know the limit: log: 5 only adds output from the Node.js side (payload, archive, resolved config). The "Updating the Application Index" step runs inside the ABAP backend — raising the log level gains you nothing there. For that you need SLG1 in client 000 on object /UI5/APPIDX, or the ADT Gateway Error Log.

title: bash: fiori: command not found when running the deploy command directly
symptom:
Running this straight in a terminal:

  npm run build && fiori deploy --config ui5-deploy.yaml --verbose

The build completes, then it stops at:

  bash: fiori: command not found
rootCause: `fiori` is a local binary installed by @sap/ux-ui5-tooling into node_modules/.bin, not on the system PATH. Only npm scripts add node_modules/.bin to PATH when they run.

solutions.label: Use npx
solutions.body: npm run build && npx fiori deploy --config ui5-deploy.yaml --verbose

solutions.label: Call the binary by path
solutions.body: npm run build && ./node_modules/.bin/fiori deploy --config ui5-deploy.yaml --verbose

solutions.label: Add a script to package.json
solutions.body:
"deploy-verbose": "npm run build && fiori deploy --config ui5-deploy.yaml --verbose"

Then just: npm run deploy-verbose

prevention: Route every project-binary command through an npm script or npx. Do not install @sap/ux-ui5-tooling globally — it drifts out of sync across team machines.

title: manifestEnhancer warning: supported locales do not contain fallback locale 'en'
symptom:
`ui5 build` prints this warning, repeated several times:

  warn builder:processors:manifestEnhancer manifest.json: Generated supported locales ('') for bundle 'i18n/i18n.properties' do not contain default fallback locale 'en'. Either provide a properties file for 'en' or configure another available fallbackLocale

The build still succeeds.
rootCause: Not verified. The project only has i18n/i18n.properties with no language suffix, while UI5 tooling derives the supported-locales list from suffixed files such as i18n_en.properties or i18n_vi.properties. The list comes out empty, so it does not contain 'en'.

solutions.label: Add an i18n_en.properties file
solutions.body:
Create webapp/i18n/i18n_en.properties (you can copy the contents of i18n.properties). Add i18n_vi.properties too if you need Vietnamese.

Side benefit: translatable text gets separated properly from the start instead of being hardcoded.

solutions.label: Configure fallbackLocale in manifest.json
solutions.body: The exact syntax for your UI5 version is not verified — check the matching UI5 documentation before applying. The idea: configure fallbackLocale under sap.ui5.models.i18n.settings to point at a locale that actually has a file.

solutions.label: Ignore it
solutions.body: The warning blocks neither the build nor the deploy. If the app is single-language with no plan for translation, it is acceptable — but it will keep adding noise to every build log.

prevention: Scaffold projects with both i18n.properties and i18n_en.properties from the template, even when translation is not yet on the roadmap.
